OCL registry statistics report thousands of active lobbyists and tens of thousands of communication reports per year. Sector concentration (pharma, telecom, energy, defence, finance) is visible in subject-matter tags. “Captured institutions” is analysis language — a logged meeting is not proof a statute was written by a lobbyist.
On the record: who registered, who was contacted, subject matter, date.

Inference (labeled): permanent multi-sector lobbying is a structural feature of Canadian federal policy. Outcome capture requires Hansard, committee, and spending instruments — not meeting counts alone.

The pharmaceutical industry is consistently among the top lobbying sectors. Drug companies lobby against PMPRB reform, against pharmacare expansion, and for extended patent protection. As documented in the regulatory capture analysis , Canada's drug prices remain among the highest in the OECD despite the PMPRB's mandate to prevent excessive pricing. Bell, Rogers, and Telus maintain active lobbying operations targeting CRTC decisions, spectrum allocations, and foreign ownership restrictions. The result: Canadians pay among the highest wireless and broadband prices in the developed world, while three companies control 87% of the wireless market. Every CRTC decision that could increase competition has been followed by intensive lobbying from…

Oil and gas companies, pipeline operators, and renewable energy firms all maintain lobbying operations. The energy sector lobbies on pipeline approvals, carbon pricing, emissions regulations, and export policy.
